\chapter{Chapter03 — Subspaces}

\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter03.SubspacesAndDecisionTrees.Subspaces}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Binary dot product form]
\lean{FABL.f₂DotProductBilin}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.𝔽₂}
\statementsource{ghsz-combinatorial-list-decoding}{pdf-6bd33ae73ade-p005-b002}
For each $n\in\mathbb{N}$, the standard dot product on the vector space
$(\mathbb{F}_2)^n$ defines a bilinear form over $\mathbb{F}_2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Bilinear form and dot product]
\lean{FABL.f₂DotProductBilin_apply}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.f₂DotProduct, FABL.f₂DotProductBilin}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $n$ and all $x,y\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$, the bilinear form given by
the coordinate dot product, evaluated at $x$ and $y$, equals their dot product in
$\mathbb{F}_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Symmetry of the binary dot product]
\lean{FABL.f₂DotProductBilin_isSymm}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.f₂DotProductBilin}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $n$, the coordinate dot product on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ is
symmetric: for all $x,y\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$, the value at $(x,y)$ equals the value at
$(y,x)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Self-orthogonality of the binary dot product]
\lean{FABL.f₂DotProductBilin_isRefl}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.f₂DotProductBilin, FABL.f₂DotProductBilin_isSymm}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $n$, every vector in $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ is orthogonal to itself
under the coordinate dot product.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nondegeneracy of the binary dot product]
\lean{FABL.f₂DotProductBilin_nondegenerate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.f₂DotProduct, FABL.f₂DotProductBilin, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $n$, the coordinate dot product on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ is
nondegenerate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Orthogonal complement of a binary subspace]
\lean{FABL.perpendicularSubspace}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p072-b004}
\label{FABL.perpendicularSubspace}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.f₂DotProductBilin, FABL.𝔽₂}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $A$ be a linear subspace of $(\mathbb{F}_2)^n$. Its
perpendicular subspace consists of the vectors whose dot product with every vector in
$A$ is zero.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $A$ be a subspace of the $n$-dimensional vector space
over $bf_2$, and let $\gamma$ be a vector in that space. Then $\gamma$ lies in the
perpendicular subspace to $A$ if and only if its dot product with every vector in $A$ is
zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Binary codimension]
\lean{FABL.f₂Codimension}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.perpendicularSubspace, FABL.𝔽₂}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p014-b003}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $A$ be a subspace of $(\mathbb{F}_2)^n$. The binary
codimension of $A$ is the dimension of its perpendicular subspace over $\mathbb{F}_2$.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $A$ be a linear subspace of the $n$-dimensional
vector space over $bf_2$. With orthogonality defined by the standard dot product over
$bf_2$, the subspace perpendicular to the subspace perpendicular to $A$ is $A$ itself.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Cardinality of a binary subspace]
\lean{FABL.card_submodule_eq_two_pow_finrank}
\label{FABL.card_submodule_eq_two_pow_finrank}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $A$ be a linear subspace of the $n$-dimensional
vector space over the field with two elements. Then the number of elements of $A$ is
$2^{\dim A}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Cardinality of the perpendicular subspace]
\lean{FABL.card_perpendicularSubspace}
\label{FABL.card_perpendicularSubspace}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.card_submodule_eq_two_pow_finrank, FABL.f₂Codimension, FABL.perpendicularSubspace, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{1}
Let $A$ be a subspace of the $n$-dimensional vector space over the field with two
elements, and let $A^\perp$ be its orthogonal subspace under the standard dot product.
If $d$ is the dimension of $A^\perp$, then $A^\perp$ has cardinality $2^d$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Subspace evaluation character]
\lean{FABL.subspaceEvaluationCharacter}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p023-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p071-b009
}
\statementsource{ghsz-combinatorial-list-decoding}{pdf-6bd33ae73ade-p005-b002}
\label{FABL.subspaceEvaluationCharacter}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.vectorWalshCharacter, FABL.vectorWalshCharacter_mul, FABL.𝔽₂}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $H$ be a subspace of $(\mathbb{F}_2)^n$, and let
$x\in(\mathbb{F}_2)^n$. The evaluation character associated with $x$ sends each
$\gamma\in H$ to the value at $x$ of the Walsh character indexed by $\gamma$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Triviality of the restricted character]
\lean{FABL.subspaceEvaluationCharacter_eq_zero_iff}
\label{FABL.subspaceEvaluationCharacter_eq_zero_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.binarySign, FABL.binarySign_eq_one_iff, FABL.f₂DotProduct, FABL.mem_perpendicularSubspace_iff, FABL.perpendicularSubspace, FABL.subspaceEvaluationCharacter, FABL.vectorWalshCharacter_apply, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $H$ be a linear subspace of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, and let
$x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$. The character on $H$ given by evaluating each vector's Walsh
character at $x$ is trivial if and only if $x$ is orthogonal to $H$ under the standard
dot product over $\mathbb{F}_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Subspace character sum]
\lean{FABL.subspaceCharacterSum}
\label{FABL.subspaceCharacterSum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.subspaceEvaluationCharacter, FABL.𝔽₂}
For a subspace $H$ of the $n$-dimensional binary cube and a point $x$ in that cube,
define the subspace character sum at $x$ to be the sum, over all $\gamma\in H$, of the
evaluation at $x$ of the character associated with $\gamma$.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $H$ be a linear subspace of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, and let
$x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$ be orthogonal to every vector in $H$ under the standard dot product
over $\mathbb{F}_2$. Then the sum over $h\in H$ of the Walsh character $(-1)^{\langle
h,x\rangle}$ is $|H|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mean of a subspace character sum]
\lean{FABL.expect_subspaceCharacterSum}
\label{FABL.expect_subspaceCharacterSum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.expect_vectorWalshCharacter, FABL.subspaceCharacterSum, FABL.subspaceEvaluationCharacter, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $H$ be a linear subspace of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, where
$\mathbb{F}_2$ is the field with two elements. The uniform expectation over
$x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$ of the sum of the characters indexed by elements of $H$, evaluated
at $x$, is $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Inverse perpendicular cardinality]
\lean{FABL.inversePerpendicularCard}
\label{FABL.inversePerpendicularCard}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.f₂Codimension, FABL.𝔽₂}
For a subspace $A$ of the $n$-dimensional binary cube, define its inverse perpendicular
cardinality to be $2^{-\operatorname{codim}(A)}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Positivity of reciprocal perpendicular size]
\lean{FABL.inversePerpendicularCard_pos}
\label{FABL.inversePerpendicularCard_pos}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.inversePerpendicularCard, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{2}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $A$ be a linear subspace of $\\mathbb F_2^n$.
The reciprocal of $2$ raised to the dimension of the orthogonal complement of $A$ (with
respect to the standard dot product) is positive.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonvanishing reciprocal perpendicular size]
\lean{FABL.inversePerpendicularCard_ne_zero}
\label{FABL.inversePerpendicularCard_ne_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.inversePerpendicularCard, FABL.inversePerpendicularCard_pos, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $A$ be a linear subspace of $\\mathbb F_2^n$.
The reciprocal of $2$ raised to the dimension of the orthogonal complement of $A$ (with
respect to the standard dot product) is nonzero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Subspace indicator formula]
\lean{FABL.setIndicator_submodule_apply}
\label{FABL.setIndicator_submodule_apply}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.card_perpendicularSubspace, FABL.f₂Codimension, FABL.inversePerpendicularCard, FABL.perpendicularSubspace, FABL.perpendicularSubspace_perpendicularSubspace, FABL.setIndicator, FABL.subspaceCharacterSum, FABL.subspaceCharacterSum_eq_card_of_mem, FABL.subspaceCharacterSum_eq_zero_of_not_mem, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{4}
For a natural number $n$, let $A$ be a linear subspace of $(\mathbf F_2)^n$, and let
$x\in(\mathbf F_2)^n$. The indicator of $A$ at $x$ equals $2^{-\operatorname{codim}(A)}$
times the sum, over all $\gamma$ perpendicular to $A$, of the character
$y\mapsto(-1)^{\sum_{i=1}^n\gamma_i y_i}$ evaluated at $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Subspace character sum Fourier vanishing]
\lean{FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_subspaceCharacterSum_of_not_mem}
\label{FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_subspaceCharacterSum_of_not_mem}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.expect_vectorWalshCharacter_mul, FABL.subspaceCharacterSum, FABL.subspaceEvaluationCharacter, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_eq_expect, FABL.vectorWalshCharacter, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $H$ be a linear subspace of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, and let
$\gamma\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$ with $\gamma\notin H$. Define a function on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$
by summing, over $y\in H$, the Walsh character indexed by $y$ and evaluated at the
argument. The Fourier coefficient of this function at $\gamma$ is zero.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $A$ be a linear subspace of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, and let
$\gamma\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$. If $\gamma$ is not orthogonal to every vector in $A$ under
the standard dot product, then the Fourier coefficient at $\gamma$ of the indicator
function of $A$ is zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Uniform probability of a binary subspace]
\lean{FABL.subspaceUniformProbability}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p072-b005}
\label{FABL.subspaceUniformProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.uniformProbability, FABL.𝔽₂}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $A$ be a subspace of $(\mathbb{F}_2)^n$. Its uniform
probability is the probability that a uniformly chosen vector in $(\mathbb{F}_2)^n$
belongs to $A$.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $A$ be a linear subspace of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$. The
probability that a uniformly chosen vector in $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ belongs to $A$ is
$2^{-d}$, where $d$ is the dimension of the perpendicular subspace $A^\perp$ under the
standard dot product over $\mathbb{F}_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Binary affine subspace]
\lean{FABL.binaryAffineSubspace}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p072-b007,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p088-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b009,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b010
}
\label{FABL.binaryAffineSubspace}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.𝔽₂}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $H$ be a subspace of $(\mathbb{F}_2)^n$, and let
$a\in(\mathbb{F}_2)^n$. The affine subspace based at $a$ with direction $H$ is the
translate $a+H$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Direction of a translated subspace]
\lean{FABL.binaryAffineSubspace_direction}
\label{FABL.binaryAffineSubspace_direction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.binaryAffineSubspace, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $H$ be a linear subspace of $\mathbb F_2^n$, and
let $a\in\mathbb F_2^n$. The direction subspace of the affine subspace $a+H$ is $H$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Membership in a binary affine subspace]
\lean{FABL.mem_binaryAffineSubspace_iff_add_mem}
\label{FABL.mem_binaryAffineSubspace_iff_add_mem}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.binaryAffineSubspace, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{4}
Let $H$ be a linear subspace of $\mathbb F_2^n$, and let $a,x\in\mathbb F_2^n$. Then $x$
belongs to the affine translate of $H$ by $a$ if and only if $x+a\in H$.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p072-b007}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{R}$, and let
$a,\gamma\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$. The Fourier coefficient at $\gamma$ of the translated
function $x\mapsto f(x+a)$ equals the Walsh character indexed by $\gamma$, evaluated at
$a$, times the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $\gamma$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Translation of an affine subspace indicator]
\lean{FABL.setIndicator_binaryAffineSubspace_eq_translate}
\label{FABL.setIndicator_binaryAffineSubspace_eq_translate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.binaryAffineSubspace, FABL.mem_binaryAffineSubspace_iff_add_mem, FABL.setIndicator, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{4}
For a natural number $n$, let $H$ be a linear subspace of $(\mathbf F_2)^n$ and let
$a\in(\mathbf F_2)^n$. For every $x\in(\mathbf F_2)^n$, the indicator of the affine
subspace $a+H$ at $x$ equals the indicator of $H$ at $x+a$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Affine subspace indicator formula]
\lean{FABL.setIndicator_binaryAffineSubspace_apply}
\label{FABL.setIndicator_binaryAffineSubspace_apply}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.binaryAffineSubspace, FABL.inversePerpendicularCard, FABL.perpendicularSubspace, FABL.setIndicator, FABL.setIndicator_binaryAffineSubspace_eq_translate, FABL.setIndicator_submodule_apply, FABL.subspaceCharacterSum, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{3}
For a natural number $n$, let $H$ be a linear subspace of the vector space $(\bbF_2)^n$,
and let $a,x\in(\bbF_2)^n$. The indicator of the affine subspace $a+H$ at $x$ equals
$2^{-\operatorname{codim}(H)}$ times the sum, over all $\gamma$ perpendicular to $H$, of
the character $y\mapsto(-1)^{\sum_{i=1}^n\gamma_i y_i}$ evaluated at $x+a$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{3}
For a natural number $n$, let $H$ be a linear subspace of $(\mathbf F_2)^n$ and let
$a\in(\mathbf F_2)^n$. For every $x\in(\mathbf F_2)^n$, the indicator of $a+H$ at $x$
equals $2^{-\operatorname{codim}(H)}$ times the sum over all $\gamma$ perpendicular to
$H$ of $(-1)^{\sum_{i=1}^n\gamma_i(x_i+a_i)}$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $H$ be a linear subspace of the $n$-dimensional vector
space over $\mathbb{F}_2$, and let $a$ and $\gamma$ be vectors in that space. If
$\gamma$ is not orthogonal to every vector in $H$ under the standard dot product, then
the Fourier coefficient at $\gamma$ of the indicator function of the affine subspace
$a+H$ is zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonemptiness of a binary affine subspace]
\lean{FABL.binaryAffineSubspace_nonempty}
\label{FABL.binaryAffineSubspace_nonempty}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.binaryAffineSubspace, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $H$ be a linear subspace of the vector space of binary
vectors of length $n$, and let $a$ be such a vector. The affine translate $a+H$ is
nonempty.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Uniform probability of an affine subspace]
\lean{FABL.affineSubspaceUniformProbability}
\label{FABL.affineSubspaceUniformProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.binaryAffineSubspace, FABL.uniformProbability, FABL.𝔽₂}
For a subspace $H$ of the $n$-dimensional binary cube and a point $a$ in that cube,
define the affine subspace uniform probability to be the uniform probability that a
point of the cube belongs to the affine subspace determined by $H$ and $a$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Affine and linear subspace probabilities]
\lean{FABL.affineSubspaceUniformProbability_eq_subspaceUniformProbability}
\label{FABL.affineSubspaceUniformProbability_eq_subspaceUniformProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.affineSubspaceUniformProbability, FABL.binaryAffineSubspace, FABL.setIndicator, FABL.setIndicator_binaryAffineSubspace_eq_translate, FABL.subspaceUniformProbability, FABL.uniformProbability, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{4}
Let $H$ be a linear subspace of $\mathbb F_2^n$ and let $a\in\mathbb F_2^n$. The
probability that a uniformly chosen vector belongs to $a+H$ equals the probability that
it belongs to $H$.
\end{theorem}

\proofstep
  {FABL.affineSubspaceUniformProbability_eq_subspaceUniformProbability}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p072-b007,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p073-b002}
\difficulty{1}
Let $H$ be a linear subspace of $\mathbb F_2^n$ and let $a\in\mathbb F_2^n$. The
probability that a uniformly chosen vector of $\mathbb F_2^n$ belongs to the affine
subspace $a+H$ is the reciprocal of $2$ raised to the dimension of the subspace
perpendicular to $H$ under the standard dot product.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.affineSubspaceUniformProbability_eq_inversePerpendicularCard}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p073-b002,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p072-b005}
\difficulty{3}
Let $H$ be a linear subspace of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, and let $a,x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$. The
uniform probability density of the affine subspace $a+H$, evaluated at $x$, equals
$\sum_{\gamma\in H^\perp}(-1)^{\langle\gamma,x+a\rangle}$, where $H^\perp$ is the
orthogonal complement under the standard dot product over $\mathbb{F}_2$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{3}
Let $H$ be a linear subspace of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ and $a\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$. As a function
of $x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$, the uniform probability density of the affine subspace $a+H$ is
$\sum_{\gamma\in H^\perp}(-1)^{\langle\gamma,x+a\rangle}$, where $H^\perp$ denotes its
orthogonal complement for the standard dot product over $\mathbb{F}_2$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $H$ be a linear subspace of the $n$-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb{F}_2$,
and let $a,\gamma$ be vectors in that space. The vector Fourier coefficient at $\gamma$
of the indicator of the affine subspace $a+H$ is nonzero if and only if $\gamma$ is
orthogonal to every vector in $H$ under the standard dot product over $\mathbb{F}_2$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $H$ be a linear subspace of the $n$-dimensional vector space over $bf_2$, and let
$a$ be a vector in that space. The indicator function of the affine subspace $a+H$ is
vector Fourier granular with granularity $2^{-\operatorname{codim}(H)}$, meaning that
each Fourier coefficient of the corresponding function on the sign cube is an integer
multiple of this number.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $H$ be a linear subspace of $\mathbb F_2^n$ and let $a\in\mathbb F_2^n$. The number
of nonzero vector Fourier coefficients of the indicator of the affine subspace $a+H$ is
$2^c$, where $c$ is the dimension of the subspace orthogonal to $H$ under the standard
dot product on $\mathbb F_2^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficient on a binary affine subspace]
\lean{FABL.abs_vectorFourierCoeff_setIndicator_binaryAffineSubspace_of_mem}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p073-b002}
\label{FABL.abs_vectorFourierCoeff_setIndicator_binaryAffineSubspace_of_mem}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.abs_vectorWalshCharacter, FABL.binaryAffineSubspace, FABL.inversePerpendicularCard, FABL.inversePerpendicularCard_pos, FABL.perpendicularSubspace, FABL.setIndicator, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_setIndicator_binaryAffineSubspace_of_mem, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{1}
Let $H$ be a linear subspace of $\mathbb F_2^n$, and let $a,\gamma\in\mathbb F_2^n$ with
$\gamma$ perpendicular to $H$ under the standard dot product. The absolute value of the
Fourier coefficient at $\gamma$ of the indicator of the affine subspace $a+H$ is the
reciprocal of $2^{\operatorname{codim}(H)}$, where $\operatorname{codim}(H)$ is the
dimension of the perpendicular subspace to $H$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{1}
Let $H$ be a linear subspace of $\mathbb F_2^n$, and let $a,\gamma\in\mathbb F_2^n$ with
$\gamma$ not perpendicular to $H$ under the standard dot product. The Fourier
coefficient at $\gamma$ of the indicator of the affine subspace $a+H$ has absolute value
zero.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $H$ be a linear subspace of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, and let
$a\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$. The sum, over all frequency vectors in $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, of the
absolute values of the Fourier coefficients of the indicator function of the affine
subspace $a+H$ is $1$.
\end{theorem}
